disposition_reason: Primary analysis of commercial fish-based baby food purees printing descriptive statistics (wet weight) for 13 elements.

study.design: Market survey of commercial fish-based baby food purees with COI DNA barcoding for species authentication and multi-element analysis
study.origin: not stated (fish species per label: sea bream, flounder, sea bass, hake, trout, salmon, cod)
study.market: pharmacies and supermarkets, Italy (commercial brands most sold in Italy)
study.method: Microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion of about 0.5 g wet sample; ICP-MS (Elan DRC-e) with Y and Re internal standards
lod: LOD mg/kg w.w.: As 0.004, Cd 0.002, Co 0.009, Cr 0.009, Cu 0.01, Hg 0.009, Mn 0.009, Ni 0.002, Pb 0.003, Sb 0.003, Se 0.003, V 0.002, Zn 0.015; LOQ = 10 x SD of blanks (values not printed)
study.qa: Duplicate per digestion batch with spike (5 mg/kg); recoveries 92-115%; no CRM reported

unresolved: Only pooled descriptive statistics across all 18 products are printed; no per-product or per-species metal values, so the effect of species substitution on metals cannot be assessed.
Arsenic is total arsenic; the risk assessment assumes inorganic arsenic is 3% of total and methylmercury is 100% of total mercury (assumptions, not measurements).
One product (9% salmon, 9% hake) failed DNA extraction; whether it was included in the 18 metal analyses is implied but not stated explicitly.
Mislabelling found by DNA barcoding: Alaska pollock and Southern hake sold as hake; rainbow trout sold as salmon (Table 1).

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Estimated daily intake from one 80 g box per day, infants 6-12 months / toddlers 1-3 years (ug/kg bw/day)

regulatory_or_exposure.value: Cd PTDI 0.357, Hg 0.229, Ni 2.8, Cr 300 ug/kg bw/day; As BMDL 0.3-8
